title: bug: messageExistsInChannel reads only the newest 1 MiB of a channel's JSONL, so chat_send's replyTo and chat_pin refuse a real message older than that (in #general, 16.5 MB, anything more than a few hours old), chat_pin with an uncoded Error, although pinMessage's comment says it "scans full JSONL, no limit"
description:
Filed by the governor from hunt #15's held items (task-928a468d, architect-1dd28c7c, msg-492975dd). Re-verified at tip f76c55f3. None of the files below changed since the repro's HEAD, d5431577.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-daemon/src/state/chatStore.ts:357-372 (messageExistsInChannel) reads `readTailJsonl(state, messagesFile, 1024 * 1024)`: only the newest 1 MiB. Its docstring (:352-355) says "Older messages cannot be referenced".
- Its pin caller contradicts that: pinMessage at chatStore.ts:522 says "Validate messageId exists in channel (scans full JSONL, no limit)".
- chat_send's replyTo check (tools/chatSend.ts:63) uses the same function.
- Live sizes at filing: #general (chan-b6d8273b.jsonl) is 16.5 MB, #governors 2.5 MB, #workers 1.5 MB. The architect measured that the newest 1 MiB of #general reached back only to about 17:57Z on 11-03, roughly 6 hours.

EFFECT
- chat_send with replyTo naming a real, older message is refused INVALID_INPUT "Invalid replyTo: message ... not found in channel".
- chat_pin of such a message is refused with a bare `Error: Message not found in channel` (chatStore.ts:524), with no MoeError code. Pinned messages are meant as durable todos and references, so pinning an older ruling is exactly the use case.

EVIDENCE
Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/me/zzHuntMe_chatTailWindow.test.ts, run at d5431577 in a snapshot outside the checkout; output in chatTailWindow.vitest.txt. One message is followed by about 1 MiB of later lines. Then both chat_send replyTo and chat_pin of the first message fail as described above.

FIX DIRECTION AND PITFALL
Give the replyTo and pin checks a lookup that covers the whole file and stays bounded in memory: a streamed scan, or a per-channel id index. Error handling: chat_pin's not-found becomes a coded MoeError.
Pitfall: chatRead.ts:120 (all-channel mode) and util/chatBacklog.ts:316 (chat_wait) also call messageExistsInChannel. There it decides whether an explicit sinceId belongs to a channel. getMessages still reads only the tail (chatStore.ts:301-306, its own TODO). A full-file "yes" there would therefore send an old sinceId into getMessages' expired-cursor fallback and replay the newest window on every call, which is what the chatBacklog comment guards against. Keep those two callers' behavior, for example with a separate full-file check used only by replyTo and pin, and pin it with a test.

FILES
chatStore.ts, possibly chatSend.ts and chatPin.ts, one vitest file, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md's `### moe.chat_send` and `### moe.chat_pin` sections (ruling msg-71db57ac). No open row holds these files at filing. Gate: the vitest file, run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout (global rail).
definitionOfDone: chat_send with replyTo naming a real message older than the newest 1 MiB of its channel succeeds, and chat_pin pins such a message (the hunt repro's two cases pass). An id the channel never had is still refused: INVALID_INPUT for chat_send, and a coded MoeError, not a bare Error, for chat_pin.
An explicit sinceId older than the read window behaves exactly as before in chat_read's all-channel mode and in chat_wait. A vitest case pins it: no newest-window replay.
The comments at chatStore.ts:352-355 and :522 and the `### moe.chat_send` and `### moe.chat_pin` sections state the real lookup bound.

Start from the architect's prototype at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-a617a035/chatMessageLookup.test.ts (158 lines, 7 cases). It ports the hunt repro /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-928a468d/me/zzHuntMe_chatTailWindow.test.ts.

Harness: ToolTestHarness, shaped like chatPin.test.ts: setupMoeFolder({ schemaVersion: 6 } as never), createEpic, workers worker-a (CODING), worker-reader and worker-peer; afterEach runs flushActivityLog, then cleanup. It imports CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES and MESSAGE_SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES from '../state/chatStore.js' (step 2 exports them). Its pushPastWindow(channel) appends worker-peer lines of about 640 bytes, in the store's own line format, until more than CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES + 64 KiB follow, and returns the newest filler id.

Cases:
(1) Only the whole-file lookup finds a message older than the window: log size > CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES, state.messageExistsInChannel is false, state.messageExistsAnywhereInChannel is true.
(2) chat_send with replyTo naming it resolves { success: true, channel }, and the stored line (found by the returned messageId via getMessages) has that replyTo. PITFALL: the hunt repro asserts `{ message: { replyTo } }`, a shape chat_send never returns (it returns { success, messageId, channel, timestamp, routingTargets }), so that case fails even with the fix. Do not copy it.
(3) chat_pin pins it: { success: true, pin: { messageId, pinnedBy: 'worker-a', done: false } }, and getPins lists it.
(4) Refusals (the error handling under test). Setup: a #general line older than the window whose replyTo and mentions hold ghost ids, plus a real #workers message. For 'msg-never-sent', the replyTo-only id, the mentions-only id and the #workers id: chat_send rejects { code: INVALID_INPUT, codeName: 'INVALID_INPUT', context: { field: 'replyTo' } }, and chat_pin rejects with an instanceof MoeError carrying { code: NOT_FOUND, codeName: 'NOT_FOUND', context: { entity: 'Message', id } }. No pin and no pins file are written.
(5) A target line starting at MESSAGE_SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES - 13, so the first chunk ends one byte into a 3-byte ✓, sitting behind a malformed padding line: the whole-file lookup finds it, the windowed one does not.
(6) chat_read all-channel mode, with workerId worker-reader, an explicit sinceId = an old #workers message, and the stored #workers cursor at the newest filler line: no #workers line comes back. After one new #workers line, exactly that line comes back, and the stored cursor is unchanged (a peek).
(7) chat_wait (channels [#workers], the same sinceId and cursor, one new line, timeoutMs 1000) delivers exactly the new line.

Cases 6 and 7 pin DoD 2: the sinceId callers' behavior is unchanged. Build them on #workers with worker-peer lines, never #general system lines: agent reads hide those as feed, which would mask a replay (mem:gotcha-chat-read-peek).

Architect RED at d1062cb0, with the constants inlined: cases 1-5 fail with the real refusals ('[INVALID_INPUT] Invalid replyTo', the bare 'Message not found in channel' Error, the missing method). Cases 6-7 pass.

implementationPlan.description:
The lookup, in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/chatStore.ts (line numbers at d1062cb0). Type it with your own editor (Edit on Claude, apply_patch on codex exec). Never `git apply`, `patch` or `cp` the prototype: a shell write leaves no TOOL witness. Reference: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-a617a035/prototype.diff.

- Import: `import { notFound } from '../util/errors.js';` (errors.ts imports nothing from state/, so there is no cycle).
- Above readTailJsonl (:261), add two exported constants:
  - `CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES = 1024 * 1024`: the newest bytes that getMessages reads and messageExistsInChannel checks. The two must agree.
  - `MESSAGE_SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES = 256 * 1024`: the whole-file scan's chunk size, exported for the test.
  getMessages (:306) and messageExistsInChannel (:363) use CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES in place of the literal `1024 * 1024`. Nothing else in them changes.
- Rewrite messageExistsInChannel's docstring (:352-356, DoD 3). It checks only the NEWEST CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES (1 MiB), the window getMessages reads, and it is bounded on purpose. chat_read's all-channel mode (chatRead.ts:120) and chat_wait's catch-up (collectChatBacklog, chatBacklog.ts:316) ask it whether getMessages can page from an explicit sinceId. An id older than the window would trip getMessages' expired-cursor fallback (:331-334) and replay the newest window on every call. Checks that must find a message whatever its age use messageExistsAnywhereInChannel. Do NOT touch chatRead.ts or chatBacklog.ts.
- Add `export function messageExistsAnywhereInChannel(state, channelId, messageId): boolean` after messageExistsInChannel:
  (a) If messageExistsInChannel finds the id, return true. Most references are recent, so the common case costs what it costs today.
  (b) Otherwise open the channel's JSONL with fs.openSync. The error handling: ENOENT returns false; any other error is thrown, because an unreadable log must not read as "no such message".
  (c) Read from offset 0 in MESSAGE_SCAN_CHUNK_BYTES chunks with fs.readSync into one reused Buffer, prefixing the carried unfinished last line. Cut lines at 0x0A bytes, which never occur inside a UTF-8 sequence, so no character is split. Decode only complete lines. At EOF (a read of 0), the carried bytes are the last line.
  (d) Pre-filter each block with Buffer.indexOf for the id as a JSON string (Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(messageId))), and JSON.parse only the lines that contain it. A match is `parsed?.id === messageId`; the same id in another line's replyTo, mentions or content is not a match. Skip a malformed line.
  (e) Close the fd in a finally.
  Memory stays at one chunk plus one line (sendMessage caps content at 10 KB). Never read the whole file into one buffer or string. The prototype puts the per-block parse in a module-private helper, blockHoldsMessage(block, needle, messageId). The docstring states the bound and the error rule.
- pinMessage (:522-525): replace the check with `if (!messageExistsAnywhereInChannel(state, channelId, messageId)) throw notFound('Message', messageId);`. Replace the 'scans full JSONL, no limit' comment with one that states the real lookup: the newest window first, then the whole JSONL.
  notFound gives code NOT_FOUND (-32001), codeName 'NOT_FOUND', the message '[NOT_FOUND] Message not found: <id>' and context { entity: 'Message', id }. The /ws PIN_MESSAGE path (WebSocketServer.ts:1130) gets the same refusal, and its catch (:1212) already adds code and codeName for a MoeError.
  Leave 'Channel not found' and 'Message already pinned' as they are (out of scope).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.chat_send's replyTo check and moe.chat_pin find a message anywhere in its channel's JSONL, whatever its age. The same holds for the board's /ws PIN_MESSAGE, which goes through pinMessage. The lookup checks the newest 1 MiB window first, then runs a synchronous chunked scan of the whole file, whose memory stays at one chunk plus one line. A reply to, or a pin of, a real message older than the newest 1 MiB (in #general, anything more than a few hours old) now succeeds. An id the channel does not hold is still refused: INVALID_INPUT (field replyTo) for chat_send, and for chat_pin a coded MoeError NOT_FOUND (context { entity: 'Message', id }) in place of a bare Error. The explicit-sinceId lookups of chat_read's all-channel mode and chat_wait's catch-up keep the windowed messageExistsInChannel. So an old sinceId still reads from the caller's stored cursor and never replays the newest window. The comments on messageExistsInChannel and on pinMessage's check, and the ### moe.chat_send and ### moe.chat_pin sections, state the real lookup bound.
acceptanceCriteria: A message is followed by more than CHAT_READ_WINDOW_BYTES of later lines. chat_send with replyTo naming it resolves success: true, the stored reply carries that replyTo, and chat_pin pins it (cases 2 and 3 of chatMessageLookup.test.ts).

For each, chat_send rejects INVALID_INPUT with context.field 'replyTo', and chat_pin rejects with a MoeError of code NOT_FOUND, codeName 'NOT_FOUND', context { entity: 'Message', id }. No pin or pins file is written (case 4).

A target line that straddles a scan chunk boundary inside a multi-byte character, behind a malformed line, is found by messageExistsAnywhereInChannel and not by messageExistsInChannel (cases 1 and 5).
chat_read all-channel mode and chat_wait, given an explicit sinceId older than the window, read from the stored cursor, with no newest-window replay (cases 6 and 7).

messageExistsInChannel's docstring, the comment on pinMessage's check, and the ### moe.chat_send and ### moe.chat_pin sections state the lookup bound. The 'scans full JSONL, no limit' comment is gone.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Switching all four callers to a whole-file lookup: rejected. chat_read's all-channel mode and chat_wait would hand an old sinceId to getMessages, whose expired-cursor fallback replays the newest window on every call. The row names this pitfall.
- A per-channel in-memory id index: rejected. It grows with the channel, needs invalidation on deleteChannel and on outside file changes, and costs a rebuild after every restart. The scan is paid only on a window miss.
- An async stream or readline scan: rejected. An early return from a for-await over a FileHandle stream risks an unhandled EBADF 'error' after close. Tool dispatch already runs under the global mutex, so async buys nothing here.
- Decoding every line (StringDecoder plus split): it works, but it is about 8x slower. On a copy of the live #general (16.7 MB), a full miss scan took 44 ms that way against 5 ms with the byte prefilter.
- Exporting the window constant makes the getMessages and messageExistsInChannel agreement explicit, since the sinceId callers depend on it, and lets the test size its fixture from it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Every chat lookup lives in state/chatStore.ts; tools reach it through the StateManager delegates.
- getMessages reads only the newest 1 MiB (its own TODO). An explicit sinceId outside that window falls back to the newest window, which is why chat_read and chat_wait ask messageExistsInChannel first (mem:gotcha-chat-read-peek).
- #general's system lines (sender system, no mentions) are feed that agent reads hide.
- The /ws ERROR frame adds code and codeName only for a MoeError.
- Tool dispatch runs under the global reentrant mutex, so a sync scan cannot interleave with a channel delete or an append.
- The live daemon runs on Windows (daemon.json projectPath D:/...). Through WSL's /mnt/d 9p mount the same scan is I/O-bound, at about 120-170 ms; that is not the daemon's cost.
planningNotes.risks:
- The hunt repro's chat_send case asserts `{ message: { replyTo } }`, which chat_send never returns, so it fails even with the fix. Case 2 asserts success plus the stored line's replyTo instead. QA should judge DoD 1 by cases 2 and 3, not by the raw repro file.
- Cases 6 and 7 must not use #general system filler: hidden feed would mask a replay. The prototype uses #workers with worker-peer lines.
- The chat_wait case skips the waiting worker's own lines, so the filler sender must not be worker-reader.
- The gate pins '(7 tests)'. Adding a case means updating the command, so keep exactly 7.
- Applying prototype.diff with git apply, patch or cp is a shell write with no TOOL witness (global rail). Type the edits with Edit/Write or apply_patch.
- Out of scope and left alone: StateManager.test.ts:2090's misleading title ('finds messages regardless of age'), and pinMessage's bare 'Channel not found' and 'Message already pinned' Errors.
- A sync scan blocks the event loop on a window miss only: about 5 ms per 16.7 MB on a native filesystem, and it grows linearly with the log.
